subject: Fast-track ask: per-tenant data residency for Meridian deal
messages:
From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fast-track ask: per-tenant data residency for Meridian deal

Team —

Quick context: Meridian Health (Ben & Asha on cc) are at final legal review and want an explicit per-tenant data residency guarantee (US-only) and an auditable export path for PHI-adjacent telemetry. This is now a gating item for their Q4 pilot signature — ARR ~ $1.2M first year.

I attached an updated MAP (Meridian_MAP_v2.pdf) with the timeline they're targeting: contract signed by 10/05, production pilot by 11/15. Legal and Security have flagged the residency clause as a must-have.

Ask: can Eng/Product evaluate whether we can (a) provide a per-tenant residency flag for hosted customers that pins data to US regions, and (b) add a scoped export endpoint with audit log hooks (not a full compliance package, but an engineering-supported export with retention metadata) — delivered as a Limited Release for Meridian within the pilot timeline?

What I need from you by EOD Thursday 16-Sep: feasibility summary (yes/no), three risk/effort bullets, and a proposal for mitigations or compensating controls if full isolation is not possible within the timeline. Meridian indicated they can accept a short-term compensating control if we provide a documented rollback plan and monthly audit extracts.

Attachments: Meridian_MAP_v2.pdf, residency-design-notes.md (draft)

Thanks — really appreciate a blunt assessment here.

—Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fast-track ask: per-tenant data residency for Meridian deal

Connor —

Thanks for the clear ask and the MAP. Quick clarifying Qs before we do a proper sizing:

1) "Per-tenant residency" — do they require physical isolation (dedicated VPC / dedicated hardware) or logical isolation (tenant flag + routing to US region racks)?
2) For the "scoped export endpoint" — what data classes must be included? Are we talking model inputs/outputs, KV cache traces, usage logs, or audit metadata only?
3) Are they expecting an SLA change (uptime/latency) tied to this residency feature?

If Meridian can accept logical isolation with strict routing + KMS-bound keys in US regions and a documented export job, rhythm-wise we might be able to do a targeted feature with an engineered guardrail. Physical isolation will push the timeline and require capacity reservation.

I'll pull in a short technical brief and a rough backlog ticket for prioritization once we have these details.

Mina
Product Lead, Platform
Redwood Inference

On Wed, 15 Sep 2026 at 09:50 AM, Asha Patel <asha.patel@meridianhealth.com> wrote:
> Hi Mina,
>
> Thanks for responding. Quick answers: Meridian is OK with logical isolation as long as (1) traffic and storage are pinned to US regions, (2) KMS keys reside in our managed US KMS, and (3) they can receive weekly audit exports including request id + model id + timestamp.
>
> We cannot accept any routing that sends data to EU/APAC even as transient cache.
>
> Best,
> Asha

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Lowe <ben.lowe@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fast-track ask: per-tenant data residency for Meridian deal

Folks —

Thanks for the details. Short technical take: logical residency (routing + regional storage + KMS in US) is feasible without dedicated hardware. Key considerations and rough effort: 

- Routing: we need a tenant-level routing flag that selects a US-only routing policy. Implementing flag + routing table changes across the serving layer: ~2-3 engineer-weeks (1 backend infra, 1 runtime change).
- Storage/KMS: ensure S3 buckets and logs are region-locked per tenant and integrate with customer-managed KMS policies. Integration + policy ops: ~1-2 engineer-weeks, but needs security review.
- Cache/Transient data: current KV cache can be sharded globally; we'd need cache-affinity to US-only nodes or ensure KV encryption with US-only persistence. This is the biggest unknown and could add 2-4 weeks if we need to carve new cache lanes.
- Export endpoint: weekly export job + audit bundle is straightforward (~1 engineer-week) if we limit scope to request id, model id, timestamps, and coarse usage metrics.

ETA: Minimum viable limited release (routing + storage + export) with compensating controls for cache would be ~4-6 weeks, assuming priority and no major security blockers. If cache affinity must be solved fully, move to 6-10 weeks.

Risks: cross-tenant routing mistakes, misconfiguration of KMS, and the cache transient path. Testing matrix required.

I can put up a short RFC and cost estimate if you want this prioritized into the next sprint cycle.

—Jonas
Eng Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

---

On Thu, 16 Sep 2026 at 12:40 PM, Ben Lowe <ben.lowe@meridianhealth.com> wrote:

>

Meridian accepts a Limited Release that includes routing + region-locked storage + weekly audit exports as long as you can commit to the pilot timeline in the MAP. Cache affinity is a known constraint we can tolerate for the pilot if you provide the compensating controls and a clear remediation schedule.
>
> Please note: our procurement team requires this in writing in the MAP (section 3.2).
>
> —Ben

Subject: Re: Fast-track ask: per-tenant data residency for Meridian deal

All —

Thanks for the quick triage. From AE perspective: if we can ship the Limited Release scope (routing + US storage + weekly export) and provide the compensating controls doc for cache transient behavior, Meridian will sign the MAP and commit to the pilot dates. They are willing to accept a clause that moves full cache affinity to a post-pilot milestone (with a credit if delayed beyond 90 days).

Can Product confirm whether we can: (1) deliver an RFCA (roadmap feature commitment agreement) that we can include in the MAP with dates, and (2) commit to a customer-visible remediation schedule in the event the cache work slips? Legal needs specific wording to include in section 3.2 and procurement is awaiting that text.

If Product/Eng can provide a one-page RFCA by Monday 20-Sep, I can get signature green-lit.

—Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
